text: How to find your IMEI code. On your phone dial *#06# and the IMEI code(s) will appear on the screen. The IMEI is also printed on the phone box and on the warranty card, and on some models under the battery. A phone with two SIM slots has two IMEI codes; check each one.

How to check whether an IMEI is registered. Open https://uzimei.uz/ and find the block 'Check the IMEI registration status'. Enter the 15-digit IMEI code and press Check. If the phone has two IMEI codes, check each one separately. One code being registered does not mean the whole device is ready.

IMEI registration tariffs (in effect from 1 August 2025). Residents and non-residents: 82,400 so'm within 30 days, 103,000 so'm after 30 days. Importers: 82,400 so'm. Local manufacturers: 41,200 so'm. Non-residents using a foreign SIM in roaming: 0 so'm. Confirm the exact amount for your application with the official operator before paying.

section: How to register a new IMEI online
text: How to register a device brought from abroad. Registration is possible only if the IMEI was cleared through customs. Online you can register only ONE IMEI, and it is reviewed within 10 days. Online customs form: https://imei.customs.uz/form-tpo . UZIMEI online registration: https://uzimei.uz/ . You can also register via the Birda app or the MyGov portal (my.gov.uz). After registering, an application number arrives by SMS; enter it to get the bank payment details.

Customs declaration for a phone. You can get the customs declaration online or at customs. Online form: https://imei.customs.uz/form-tpo . If the customs declaration lists both IMEIs of a dual-SIM phone, you can register the second IMEI online too; if only one IMEI is listed, register the second one at a UZIMEI registration office.

section: Second IMEI of a dual-SIM phone
text: A phone with two SIM slots has two IMEI codes. If the customs declaration records both IMEIs, you may register the second IMEI online as well. If the declaration records only one IMEI, register the second one in person at a UZIMEI registration office.

section: Register in person at an operator
text: Registering IMEI in person. Go to a UZIMEI operator with your passport (or a document matching your status), the device, and a local subscriber number in the applicant's name. Residents: passport, a number in the applicant's name, the device, an application form and payment. Foreign citizens: ask about the accepted document at the call centre 1170. Find registration points on https://uzimei.uz/?id=map . Give original documents only to the official registrar, never to a chat.

Finding a nearby registration point. Open 'Support centre' then 'Our addresses' on uzimei.uz, choose your region or city, and the registration points block will show the offices. If the exact office or opening hours are unclear, confirm on 1170 before travelling.

section: MNP - transfer a number to another operator
text: MNP (mobile number portability) lets you keep your phone number when moving to another operator. Ordinary porting is done once. After a local SIM is activated, 30 calendar days apply before another transfer. If your application was rejected, common reasons are: data mismatch, debt to the previous operator, less than 30 days since the last transfer, or the number being blocked.

section: Does the balance transfer with MNP
text: Money on the account is not carried over automatically when porting a number between operators. Spend or check your balance with the current operator before transferring.

If your phone is lost or stolen, file an application with the Internal Affairs Department (police). The application should include the device manufacturer, model and IMEI codes. UZIMEI cannot track or block a device for you.

If the device is blocked or the network does not work, first turn the phone off and on and check the connection. A device tied to an old subscriber number is a separate case. Do not promise that a simple repayment fixes it; check the exact case with the operator or call 1170.

TAC is the first 8 digits of the IMEI and identifies the device type and manufacturer. If the device type or TAC does not match, resolve it with the manufacturer. Never change a device's IMEI code yourself. For routers, modems or watches, check the device-type FAQ; if the type is not recognised, call 1170.

section: IMEI registration payment vs customs payment
text: The UZIMEI registration fee and the customs payment are two different payments. Do not count the UZIMEI tariff instead of the customs payment. Confirm the amount for your specific application with the official operator before paying.

For help you can call the UZIMEI support number 1170, or use the support centre on https://uzimei.uz/contacts . The assistant cannot register an official appeal or accept personal/confidential data; fill official screens yourself.
